title: Google Makes Visible Gemini Media Watermarks Optional
summary: Gemini users can remove visible marks from generated images, video and music, while Google retains invisible SynthID provenance.
body:
## Visible labels become a user choice

Google has begun allowing Gemini users to decide whether creations made with its image, video and music generators carry a visible watermark. The change is rolling out over several days and removes a mark that was previously embedded prominently in much of the media produced through Gemini.

Google is not abandoning machine-readable provenance. The company says generated media will continue to contain invisible SynthID watermarks, which are designed to survive ordinary transformations and can be detected by Google’s verification systems. Users can ask Gemini whether an uploaded image, video or piece of music was generated by Google AI. The detector therefore answers a narrower question than universal AI-content detection: it checks for Google’s own provenance signal rather than proving whether any model from any provider created the file.

The decision extends an approach Google had already used selectively for professional products. Some higher-tier and developer workflows previously omitted visible marks to provide clean production assets while retaining SynthID. Making that choice available more broadly shifts Gemini toward the expectations of creators, advertisers and businesses that do not want a platform logo baked into finished work.

## Provenance moves into the infrastructure

Removing mandatory visible marks creates an obvious tradeoff. Casual viewers lose an immediate warning when synthetic media is reposted without context, while publishers gain material that does not require cropping or retouching. Invisible identification is less intrusive, but it only protects the information environment if platforms, newsrooms and users have ready access to reliable detection tools.

The change matters because Google operates consumer creation tools across several media formats at global scale. Its policy can influence what users come to expect from competing generators: clean output at the surface, with provenance carried underneath. It also puts more weight on SynthID’s durability and availability. If invisible watermark checks remain confined to particular services, the practical transparency provided by Gemini media may decline even though the underlying signal is still present.
title_zh: 谷歌开放关闭Gemini可见水印，SynthID仍将保留
summary_zh: Gemini将允许用户关闭图片、视频和音乐作品上的可见水印，但谷歌仍会嵌入不可见的SynthID来源标记。
body_zh:
## 可见标识改由用户决定

谷歌开始允许Gemini用户自行决定，使用其图片、视频和音乐生成工具创作的内容是否显示可见水印。该功能将在数日内逐步上线，此前出现在大量Gemini生成媒体上的醒目标记将不再强制保留。

谷歌并未放弃机器可识别的来源信息。公司表示，生成内容仍会嵌入不可见的SynthID水印。这类标记被设计为能够承受常见的压缩和编辑处理，并可由谷歌的验证系统识别。用户还可以把图片、视频或音乐上传到Gemini，询问它是否由谷歌AI生成。需要注意的是，这项检测解决的是一个较窄的问题：它寻找谷歌自己的来源信号，并不能判断文件是否由其他公司的模型制作。

谷歌此前已经在部分专业产品中采取类似做法。某些高阶订阅和开发工具可以输出没有可见标记的素材，同时保留SynthID。如今把选择权扩大到更多Gemini用户，意味着产品开始贴近创作者、广告主和企业的实际需求——他们通常不希望成品中永久带有平台标志。

## 来源标识转向底层基础设施

取消强制可见水印也带来明显取舍。合成内容脱离原始发布环境后，普通观看者将失去一眼可见的提醒；另一方面，发布者不必再裁切或修补水印。不可见标识对画面干扰更小，但只有当平台、媒体机构和公众能够方便地调用可靠检测工具时，它才足以维护信息透明度。

这项变化之所以重要，是因为谷歌面向全球提供跨图片、视频和音乐的消费级生成工具。其选择可能影响行业默认规则：用户在表面上获得干净素材，来源信息则下沉到文件和检测基础设施中。与此同时，SynthID的抗破坏能力和检测工具的开放程度将变得更加关键。如果验证能力长期局限在少数谷歌服务内，即使底层标记仍然存在，Gemini生成内容在现实传播中的透明度也可能下降。
